name: Sungor
confidence_why: The only statement on Sungor stress is the survey line in Tucker and Bryan 1966, drawing on Lukas 1938, that nothing is known about stress, and the two first-hand descriptions, Lukas 1938 and Guinet 1973, exist only in print, so no stress rule can be given for Sungor.

The bracketed elision covers the example forms ("Lexical tone: TAMA uti grass; tutu ear; MARARIT tdk why?; tok ten; i woman; i thou. Grammatical tone: TAMA t…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule: the survey covering the Tama group (Tama, Sungor, Mararit) reports lexical and grammatical tone for Tama and probably Mararit and states explicitly that nothing is known about stress; no Sungor-specific tone or stress data are given. Wikipedia (citing Edgar 1990/1991) adds that Sungor is 'most likely' tonal with H and L, but that is not a stress statement.
new_statements.domain_note: Group-level statement about the whole Tama group, not Sungor specifically; drawn from Stevenson's MS notes (Tama, Mararit) and Lukas 1938 (Sungor). It records absence of knowledge, not absence of stress. Not a first-hand description; the first-hand descriptions (Guinet 1973 phonology sketch, Lukas 1938 grammar sketch) were not openable.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog assa1269 'Assangori' = Sungor/Asongori/Asungor (ISO sjg), with dialects Erenga, Girga, Murasi, Sebunkik, Sungor, Walad Dulla. Lukas 1938 and Guinet 1973 describe 'Sungor' (Chadian Wadai variety); the Tucker & Bryan 1966 statement is for the whole Tama group (Tama tama1331, Mararit, Sungor), and its Sungor data come from Lukas 1938.

tone.says: Dedicated phonology sketch of Sungor (assa1269), the closest sister of Tama; Guinet's Sungor forms as re-quoted from it in Edgar 1991 / Starostin's GLD carry H and L tone marks with tonal plural alternations (e.g. kìdì-k pl. kìdí-ŋé 'black', kíŋá-t pl. kìŋá-k 'bone', úfùr-ɲà-t 'bark'), so the sketch records tone; Tama proper enters only as comparanda (GLD source list: '[Gn.] = X. Guinet. (A) Tama. Published in: Esquisse d'une phonologie du sungor'); the tone section itself was not s…
